mode: Style transfer from existing project machinery
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: production 2D side-view game sprite atlas on a genuinely transparent background.
Redesign the supplied existing machinery atlas (image 1) into a NEW exterior bunker-defense component atlas. Image 1 is the rendering/material/palette reference; image 2 is an additional worn-steel surface reference. Preserve the detailed gritty industrial pixel-rendered style of image 1, its fine mottled metal, rust, riveted edges, little warm brass fasteners, near-black occlusion and warm upper-left edge light. Replace the objects with the following EIGHT complete isolated components.
Layout: exactly FOUR COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, eight equal cells, landscape canvas. Every sprite centered in its own cell with generous fully transparent margins. No labels, letters, numbers, separators, surrounding scene or ground plane.
Top row left to right:
1. Narrow retractable FIELD WIRE BARRIER, seen in the game's orthogonal SIDE ELEVATION, almost edge-on across the player's horizontal movement lane. A compact weathered steel lattice panel with taut and slightly bent wire mesh, narrow dark steel end posts, bolted diagonal brace and a shallow heavy sliding cassette foot. Width of upright portion about half its height. Actual transparent holes in mesh. Not a broad front-facing garden gate, no door handle.
2. Narrow retractable CONCRETE BARRIER in exactly the same side-elevation proportions: heavy concrete cross-section, chipped stone aggregate and rusted embedded reinforcement, steel guide runners, dirty battered shallow cassette foundation. Upright width about half its height. Restrained cold grey-brown, not bright white.
3. Narrow retractable ARMORED STEEL BARRIER with the same proportions and ground anchor: thick staggered worn olive-dark steel plates, recessed bolts, layered edge thickness, an external piston/guide rail, modest brass joints. No door, handle, window or generic green rectangle.
4. Heavy stationary GROUND-SENTRY PEDESTAL only, NO gun and NO tripod placed on top: narrow enclosed mechanical support with thick load-bearing bracing, cast swivel bearing at the TOP, protected drive motor, side ammo/service box, bundled cable, broad squat anchored foot. Height about twice width. This supports a gun at its top 108 game pixels above ground. Credible mass and construction, no thin line-frame watchtower.
Bottom row left to right:
5. Heavy stationary ANTI-AIR PEDESTAL only, NO gun: related but visibly different squat-tapered hydraulic column, ribbed bolted column and geared bearing at top, mechanical traverse housing, side ammo box, grounded anchor feet. Similar height and width to component 4, distinct reinforced mechanism.
6. Separate TWIN ANTI-AIR BARREL AND BREECH assembly facing exactly RIGHT, horizontal side elevation, pivot near LEFT third. Two long parallel perforated barrels, heavy weathered breech and recoil cylinders, a compact shaped armored mantlet which exposes the mechanism. No pedestal, no huge flat shield, no people, no muzzle flash.
7. Low pile of DESTROYED BARRIER DEBRIS: compact broken concrete chunks, twisted rebar and bent dark steel, heavy fragments resting on one shared horizontal baseline, low height, no particles.
8. WRECKED PEDESTAL BASE: broken bolted anchor foot and short bent industrial support, exposed cables, crushed ammo housing, no intact gun, resting on the same horizontal baseline.
Camera/style invariants: the 2D side-scroller camera is level and looks at the side of machinery; all verticals remain vertical and the ground baseline is horizontal. Only restrained local edge thickness as in image 1; no aerial view, no isometric view, no receding floor. Match fine texture density and rough material shading to the original machinery, not coarse vector blocks, flat icons, cartoon outlines or smooth plastic renders. Each part must remain legible when reduced to roughly 40–75 pixels wide in game. Keep silhouette edges crisp. Transparent background and transparent mesh holes, absolutely no black backing rectangle, checkerboard, colored glow, soft halo, vignette or diffuse outer shadow. All pieces fully visible, safely separated and not touching cell edges.
notes: Original generated alpha is preserved. Runtime atlas regions and anchors are defined in scripts/perimeter_art.gd. Pixel filtering and a small alpha cutoff suppress only faint extraction fringes. Existing machine-gun barrel is reused from the original machinery atlas.
